issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I wanted to publish multiple resource slices within the same pool, but there was no easy way to do this with the recommended helper library.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the API to `draplugin.PublishResources()` to take a list of ResourceSlices, similar to the call to `resourceslice.Update()` that it wraps. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Examine the code here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin/draplugin.go#L427-L459
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin/draplugin.go#L410

This is an oversight. Ideally we should fix this quickly and backport to v1.32.1 for DRA drivers targeting 1.32.

Should we modify the original API interface or add a new one? 🤔 
like this: 
`PublishMultipleResources(ctx context.Context, resourcesList []Resources) error`

We can just change the existing Go API. It means that DRA drivers need to be updated when bumping their dependencies from v1.32.0 to v1.32.1, but that's okay: the k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation module has version v0.32.0 resp. v0.32.1, i.e. no API stability guarantee.

Between 0.32.0 and 0.33.0? It's normal Go practice that there there is no API stability for 0.x releases. While we strive for more stability in staging repos, we also have always reserved the right to change APIs if needed. This one falls into that category.

Actually, it's even [documented explicitly already](https://github.com/kubernetes/dynamic-resource-allocation?tab=readme-ov-file#compatibility)! :smile:

Or did you mean between patch releases (major.minor.patch), i.e. 0.32.0 and 0.32.1?

While unusual, "no compatibility guarantees" also extends to patch releases.

Kubernetes compatibility rules are much stricter as you can see in the backport rules, https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-release/cherry-picks.md

I don't see anything in that document about "don't break APIs".

I fully understand that this would be surprising and that it might not be important enough for a backport, but in this case forgetting to update that API in 1.32.0 is the bug that we want to fix.

Okay, let's not backport.

review_comments:
Yes. The name used for the pool should represent the "grouping" of resource slices that are part of that pool. 

When talking about node-local resources, the logical pool boundary is the set of resourceSlices for a given node (i.e. for a given driver, there will be multiple pools -- one per node).

When talking about non-node-local resources, a different name should to be used (but it still needs represent the logical grouping of resources from multiple resourceslices that are contained in that pool).

For example, in the case of allocating IMEX channels by our NVIDIA DRA driver, we use the name of the IMEX domain as the pool name:
https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-dra-driver/blob/main/cmd/nvidia-dra-controller/imex.go#L190

At present there is only 1 resourceSlice per pool, but if we ever wanted to support more than 128 IMEX channels per IMEX domain, then we would need multiple resourceSlices for the same IMEX domain, and that grouping would be encoded by the fact that all of the resourceSlices associated with a given IMEX domain have the same pool name.
Thanks for the reply, it gave me a better understanding of this aspect.
Why do we pass a context at all if it is never used?

Indeed, `PublishResources` is asynchronous update and return immediately. It seems that there is no need to use ctx to set a timeout or cancel the call. In addition, draPlugin itself also has backgroundCtx, which should be able to be deleted.  @pohly
Because it's more future-proof. If at some point we do need a context (for example, for contextual logging), then adding it would be another API break.
